discussion_comments.comment_body:
Good catch — fixed in b6491cf4d. This one mattered more than it looks, because the failure mode you describe is the exact one the `basicAuth` support in this PR exists to prevent: a silently-dropped credential field means the scrape runs unauthenticated, Bifrost returns `401`, and the target sits at `up=0` with no error anywhere. Leaving `authorization` structurally open re-opened that hole from the other side.

- `authorization` now matches the ServiceMonitor `SafeAuthorization` shape: `type`, plus a `credentials` selector with `name` and `key` **required** and `optional` allowed. Closed with `additionalProperties: false`. (Deliberately no `credentialsFile` — that's on the non-safe `Authorization` type used by Probe, not on ServiceMonitor endpoints.)
- `relabelings` and `metricRelabelings` now reference a shared closed `relabelConfig` definition in `$defs` covering `sourceLabels`, `separator`, `targetLabel`, `regex`, `modulus`, `replacement`, and `action`.

Both typos you named are now rejected at validation time:

```
$ helm template rel . --set serviceMonitor.enabled=true \
    --set serviceMonitor.authorization.credentails.name=tok
Error: at '/serviceMonitor/authorization': additional properties 'credentails' not allowed

$ helm template rel . --set serviceMonitor.enabled=true \
    --set 'serviceMonitor.metricRelabelings[0].sourceLables[0]=__name__'
Error: at '/serviceMonitor/metricRelabelings/0': additional properties 'sourceLables' not allowed
```

I left `action` as a free-form string rather than an enum. The operator's accepted actions have grown over time (`keepequal` / `dropequal` are relatively recent) and are matched case-insensitively, so pinning an enum here would age into rejecting valid configs — whereas a wrong `action` value surfaces loudly in the operator rather than silently, unlike a misspelled field name. Verified the documented `metricRelabelings` drop example and a full `hashmod` config (all seven fields) still pass.
base_key in config.schema.json has no additionalProperties: false, so the runtime accepts use_anthropic_endpoints on any provider key
